repo_rules.title: Locked dependency graph
repo_rules.rationale: A declared manifest without a lock, digest, or equivalent resolution record leaves the build dependent on future registry state.
repo_rules.next_step: Commit the ecosystem's resolution record and verify it in CI; review generated or vendored dependencies separately.

repo_rules.title: Configuration contract
repo_rules.rationale: Templates and schemas make deploy-time inputs discoverable without committing deploy-specific values or secrets.
repo_rules.next_step: Publish a secret-free configuration example or schema and document startup validation and failure behavior.

repo_rules.title: Immutable build and release path
repo_rules.rationale: A repeatable build or release definition is the starting evidence for separating build, release, and run.
repo_rules.next_step: Build once in CI, identify the artifact immutably, attach configuration later, and promote the same bytes between environments.

repo_rules.title: Production-significant test path
repo_rules.rationale: Tests and CI provide review leads for production-significant differences, but only a human can confirm that the important differences are actually exercised.
repo_rules.next_step: Name production-only differences explicitly and exercise them in representative integration, system, or end-to-end tests.

repo_rules.title: Auditable administrative procedures
repo_rules.rationale: Administrative work should be versioned, repeatable, bounded, and run from the same release context as the application.
repo_rules.next_step: Put migrations, repair commands, and runbooks under review with dry-run, authorization, and audit behavior.

repo_rules.title: Machine-readable interface contracts
repo_rules.rationale: Schemas and interface descriptions make consumer-visible behavior reviewable before and alongside implementation.
repo_rules.next_step: Publish the relevant OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Protocol Buffer, JSON Schema, GraphQL, or typed interface contract and test semantic compatibility.

repo_rules.title: Security policy and safe reporting path
repo_rules.rationale: A security policy is not proof of secure design, but it exposes ownership, reporting, and response expectations.
repo_rules.next_step: Add SECURITY.md, threat-model the public boundaries, and test authentication, authorization, abuse, and fail-closed behavior.

repo_rules.title: Service-level and observability evidence
repo_rules.rationale: Instrumentation and objectives should connect telemetry to user-visible risk rather than merely collecting logs.
repo_rules.next_step: Define user-visible SLIs/SLOs, instrument causal context, and document which alerts require action.

repo_rules.title: Supply-chain verification evidence
repo_rules.rationale: Dependency automation, SBOMs, attestations, and provenance workflows are evidence that artifact admission is deliberate.
repo_rules.next_step: Pin third-party automation, generate an SBOM, sign or attest releases, and verify provenance before deployment.

repo_rules.title: Fault-containment evidence
repo_rules.rationale: Resilience requires explicit bounds and recovery tests, not an untested claim that the platform is highly available.
repo_rules.next_step: Document timeout, retry, queue, load, and blast-radius bounds; add a tested recovery or fault-injection path.

repo_rules.title: Data lifecycle and privacy policy
repo_rules.rationale: Retention, deletion, export, and privacy documents expose whether every copy has an owner and an end-of-life path.
repo_rules.next_step: Map collection through deletion, including backups, analytics, logs, exports, replicas, and derived data.

repo_rules.title: Reviewed infrastructure or policy as code
repo_rules.rationale: Declarative infrastructure and policy files create a reviewable desired state and a place to define safe reconciliation.
repo_rules.next_step: Version desired state, validate policy before apply, detect drift, and require explicit approval for destructive reconciliation.

repo_rules.title: Progressive exposure controls
repo_rules.rationale: Feature flags, canary policy, or staged deployment definitions are review leads for separating deployment from exposure.
repo_rules.next_step: Define cohorts, health gates, automatic stop conditions, rollback behavior, and cleanup ownership for exposure controls.

repo_rules.title: Compatibility and migration evidence
repo_rules.rationale: Changelogs, migrations, compatibility tests, and deprecation records make coexistence and rollback reviewable.
repo_rules.next_step: Specify support windows, additive change rules, migration checkpoints, rollback, and the evidence required before removal.

repo_rules.title: Outcome ownership evidence
repo_rules.rationale: CODEOWNERS and contribution guidance identify review responsibility, but a human must still verify end-to-end outcome authority.
repo_rules.next_step: Name an empowered team that owns the user outcome, operations, safety, cost, change, and retirement—not only a component.

repo_rules.title: Cost attribution and budget evidence
repo_rules.rationale: Budgets, unit economics, and cost runbooks provide evidence that resource use is treated as an architectural boundary.
repo_rules.next_step: Attribute spend to user-visible units, set budget and anomaly boundaries, and include cost in design and incident review.

repo_rules.title: Sustainable operation evidence
repo_rules.rationale: Sustainability records provide a place to connect useful work to energy, hardware, data movement, and lifecycle decisions.
repo_rules.next_step: Measure material impact, reduce waste without exporting harm, and record the trade-offs alongside performance and cost.

manual_rules.title: Replaceable backing-service contracts
manual_rules.rationale: Static files cannot establish that backing services are attached through explicit, replaceable contracts.
manual_rules.next_step: Review binding, identity, timeout, migration, failure, and replacement behavior for every backing service.

manual_rules.title: Stateless execution boundary
manual_rules.rationale: Repository evidence alone cannot prove that durable state is kept behind explicit contracts at runtime.
manual_rules.next_step: Terminate or relocate instances and verify correctness, session continuity, and durable state ownership.

manual_rules.title: Bounded concurrency model
manual_rules.rationale: A code scan cannot reliably infer queue, worker, thread, connection, and downstream saturation bounds.
manual_rules.next_step: Document each concurrency layer, its admission and backpressure rules, and the test that proves overload remains bounded.

manual_rules.title: Startup and shutdown correctness
manual_rules.rationale: Disposability is a runtime property that requires termination and recovery evidence.
manual_rules.next_step: Measure readiness, drain in-flight work, test abrupt termination, and prove retry or replay does not corrupt outcomes.
